about: Where both apps cut a spoken answer into pieces. Written by hand, not generated: this is app-side text handling, with no backend answer to record. Read by jarvis-desktop/tests/speech-pieces.mjs (src/speech-pieces.js) and jarvis-client SpeechTextTest.kt (voice/SpeechText.kt). Each test feeds `text` to its app's cutter the way the app does while an answer streams in - all at once, and again one character at a time, each call starting where the last one stopped and treating it as the first piece while nothing has been cut - then adds what is left at the end, trimmed, as the app does when the answer is over. Both must give `pieces` exactly. The numbers and the word list below must be the ones each app uses.

cases.name: the first piece ends at its first comma; the rest are sentences
cases.text: Tomorrow looks mild, with light rain in the afternoon. It should clear up by the evening, and stay dry.
pieces: with light rain in the afternoon.
It should clear up by the evening, and stay dry.

cases.name: only the first piece is cut early
cases.text: Tomorrow looks mild, with rain, and wind. Later, it clears up, mostly.

cases.name: a comma with fewer than 10 characters before it is not a cut
cases.text: Well, it depends on the weather. Maybe tomorrow.
pieces: Well, it depends on the weather.

cases.name: no cut after a word a speaker would not pause after
cases.text: You can take the bus and, if it rains, a taxi.
pieces: You can take the bus and, if it rains,

cases.name: a thousands separator is not a cut
cases.text: It costs 1,450 dollars, which is a lot.

cases.name: a time is not a cut; a colon with a space after it is
cases.text: Meet at 10:30 in the lobby, near the lifts.

cases.name: a colon before a list
cases.text: Here are the three options: walk, bus or taxi.

cases.name: a semicolon
cases.text: The shop is closed today; it opens at nine tomorrow.

cases.name: a web address is not a cut
cases.text: The page is at https://example.com/a,b for now, I think.
pieces: The page is at https://example.com/a,b for now,

cases.name: a short sentence first is still the first piece
cases.text: Sure. The weather tomorrow, as far as I know, is mild.
pieces: The weather tomorrow, as far as I know, is mild.

cases.name: no punctuation: cut after 12 words
cases.text: One two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen.
pieces: One two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve

cases.name: no punctuation: after 12 words, the first word that is not one to avoid
cases.text: This is a very long opening with no punctuation at all in it so we cut here.
pieces: This is a very long opening with no punctuation at all in it so we cut

cases.name: a comma not yet followed by anything waits; the end of the answer says the rest
an answer that is one short phrase
a comma after a capital I is avoided like a lowercase one
cases.text: The one you and I, as it happens, both like.
pieces: The one you and I, as it happens,

cases.name: leading blank lines do not stop the first piece
